requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version when resolving a system update.
requirements.summary: curl began at 0:8.9.1-5.el10. A version lock for that exact NEVRA was installed, while an unlocked check showed 8.12.1 available. A full 279-package upgrade simulation excluded curl, and curl remained at the original version after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel.
requirements.summary: The system retained redhat-release 10.0-30.el10 and kernel-core 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; the same kernel remained running after the verified restart. The fixed lifecycle platform snapshots independently agree.

requirements.requirement: Use software compatible with the existing legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The executor installed only the RHEL 10 repository-provided version-lock plugin at 4.7.0-8.el10, matching the existing DNF plugin suite, and package health remained good afterward.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node1 restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and system services, curl integrity, package versions, and the persistent lock recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations corroborate the boot transition and unchanged platform.
limitations: The full system update was validated with DNF's transaction simulation rather than applied. This is strong evidence that curl was excluded while avoiding prohibited OS and kernel upgrades, but it does not observe a completed full update transaction.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the version-lock plugin and adding the curl lock directly implemented the task; temporary simulation files were removed; the restart was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. The unsuccessful timer-status observation was read-only and occurred while the node restarted. Final observations show no failed services, no unexpected listeners or temporary residue, and a healthy package manager.
